title: BACS: first reports of successful cyberattacks on Swiss companies carried out with AI agents
date_note: Both pages give only their publication day (25 November 2026); the attack dates are not stated.
geo_basis: Federal agency that reported it (BACS, Bern); victims are not named
summary: Switzerland’s Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) says it has for the first time received reports of successful cyberattacks on companies and critical-infrastructure operators in which attackers used AI agents. Inside-IT quotes BACS saying that in all the attacks known to it the AI agents led to a successful compromise. BACS says the agents exploit weak or default passwords and known vulnerabilities, and expects such fast attacks to become more frequent.
plain: Switzerland’s cyber office says AI agents were used for the first time in successful attacks on Swiss companies and critical-infrastructure operators, exploiting weak passwords and known flaws.
exec: BACS reports AI-agent attacks that succeeded against Swiss companies and infrastructure operators, and expects more of them.
action: BACS advises installing critical security updates on internet-facing systems as quickly as possible, no later than after 24 hours.
impact: Victims are not named and the pages read give no total number of attacks.

validation.note: Netzwoche and Inside-IT, two Swiss publishers, each report the BACS communication on the first successful AI-agent attacks in Switzerland. The BACS press release itself was not found or read.
